rows.why: S1 depends on what the default share is (7500 of 10000). Item 3 covers which share values are valid and what unit they use, but no item asks for the default value.

Item 1 asks how the hidden-test share is rounded. The pick rounds down with BigInt integer division and gives the remainder to UAT, so 999 gives 749 and 250. BigInt keeps the amounts exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Item 8 asks what the remaining balance released on UAT approval is. The pick releases the bounty minus the hidden-test share, which is the rest of the balance and marks the task fully released.
Item 7 asks what a failed hidden-test run does to the state. The pick saves nothing and returns the current state, so the task stays locked.

Item 6 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. The pick rejects with an Error and records nothing, as S5 expects. The pick doesn't give the error's wording, but the behaviour matches.
Item 9 asks how a zero bounty behaves. The pick reports 'pro bono' but still records releases of 0, while S6 says no release is ever recorded.
Item 5 asks about a redelivered event or a second event of the same kind. The pick writes nothing in both cases, which matches both parts of S7.
Item 11 asks how concurrent events are handled. The pick runs events one at a time through a promise queue, so the second event sees the first release and exactly one release is recorded.
Item 11 also asks how store failures are handled. The pick passes on the store's error and leaves the queue usable, so the same event can be retried and succeed.
